root_cause.summary: An LLM replacement could succeed before later STT convergence failed. The old LLM signature and its deferred retry bookkeeping could then remain stale. Returning A to B to A compared desired A against cached A and skipped a replacement although the installed immutable request provider was bound to B.
root_cause.warmup_distinction: Preparing a runtime from current canonical settings does not replace the provider's immutable backend/device/spec binding. Requested profile and effective execution backend remain distinct, including legitimate E4B internal GPU-to-CPU fallback.
root_cause.before_proof: The original native safety attempts were retained by managed-execution. They were not rerun to confirm their failure during this repair. This record supplies controlled post-repair evidence, not native acceptance after-proof.

behavior: LlmProviderRebuildOwner commits an LLM-only signature immediately after successful provider replacement, before usage refresh and later STT work.
Construction yielding no provider or replacement raising marks the existing retry state immediately; the failed requested profile is not stamped as successfully applied.
Provider runtime convergence success synchronizes STT signatures separately and cannot overwrite the failed-LLM retry marker.
The existing combined signature synchronization and () retry-marker consumer remain available for their existing callers; no new retry-state field was introduced.
A settings transaction may remain committed/runtime-degraded for STT failure while the independently successful LLM binding is retained and correctly used by subsequent requests.
preserved: No unapplied STT signature is published after STT convergence failure.
No degraded transaction is relabeled as wholly applied.
No force-all-rebuild policy or dynamic desired-backend lookup per request.
No execution guard bypass, prefix-refresh predicate change, inference profile change or model substitution.
No edits to translation_enable.py, control_repair_behavior.py or overlay tests.
